mn13:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.
mn13:2.1: Then, it being morning, a number of bhikkhus dressed, and taking their bowls and (outer) robes, they went into Sāvatthi for alms.
mn13:2.3: ‘It is still too early to wander for alms in Sāvatthi;
mn13:2.4: suppose we went to the Other Sectarian Wanderers’ Park? ’
mn13:2.5: So they went to the Other Sectarian Wanderers’ Park, and they exchanged greetings with the Other Sectarian Wanderers,
mn13:2.6: and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, they sat down at one side. When they had done so, the Wanderers said to them:
mn13:3.1: ‘Friends, the Monk Gotama makes known full-knowledge of sensual desires, and so too do we;
mn13:3.2: the Monk Gotama makes known full-knowledge of form, and so too do we;
mn13:3.3: the Monk Gotama makes known full-knowledge of feelings, and so too do we.
mn13:3.4: What then is the distinction here, what is the variance, what is the difference between the Monk Gotama’s teaching of the Dhamma and ours,
mn13:4.1: Then without agreeing or disagreeing with these words,
mn13:4.2: the bhikkhus got up from their seats and went away,
mn13:4.3: (thinking:) ‘We shall come to know the meaning of these words in the Blessed One’s presence.’
mn13:5.1: When they had wandered for alms in Sāvatthi and had returned from their alms-round after the meal, they went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, they sat down at one side. When they had done so, they told him what had taken place.
mn13:6.1: ‘Bhikkhus, wanderers of other sects who say thus should be questioned thus:
mn13:6.2: “But, friends, what is the gratification, what is the danger, and what is the escape, in the case of sensual desire?
mn13:6.3: What is the gratification, what is the danger, and what is the escape, in the case of form?
mn13:6.4: What is the gratification, what is the danger, and what is the escape, in the case of feelings?”
mn13:6.5: Being questioned thus wanderers of other sects will fail to account for the matter, and what is more, they will get into difficulties.
mn13:6.7: Because it is not their province.
mn13:6.8: Bhikkhus, I see no one in the world with its gods, its Māras and Divinities, in this generation with its monks and divines, with its kings and its men, who could satisfy the mind a reply to these questions, unless it were a Tathāgata or a Tathāgata’s disciple, or else one who has learnt it from that (source).
mn13:7.1: (i) ‘And what is gratification in the case of sensual desires?
mn13:7.2: ‘Bhikkhus, there are these five cords of sensual desires.
mn13:7.4: Forms cognizable through the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative, of lust.
mn13:7.8: Tangibles cognizable through the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likable, connected with sensual desires, and provocative of lust.
mn13:7.9: These are the five cords of sensual desire.
mn13:7.10: ‘Now the pleasure and joy that arise dependent on those five cords of sensual desire are the gratification in the case of sensual desires.
mn13:8.1: (ii) ‘And what is the danger in the case of sensual desires?
mn13:8.2: ‘Here, bhikkhus, on account of the calling by which a clansman makes a living,
mn13:8.3: whether checking or accounting or calculating or ploughing or trading or cattle farming or archery or as a king’s man, or whatever the calling may be,
mn13:8.4: he has to face cold, he has to face heat, he is harassed by mosquitoes and flies, wind and sun and creeping things, risking death by hunger and thirst.
mn13:8.5: ‘Now this danger in the case of sensual desires, (this) mass of suffering visible here and now, has sensual desires for its reason, sensual desires for its source, sensual desires for its cause, the reason being simply sensual desires.
mn13:9.1: ‘If no property comes to the clansman while he works and strives and makes efforts thus,
mn13:9.2: he sorrows, grieves and laments, beating his breast he weeps till he is distraught,
mn13:9.3: (crying:) “My work is vain, my work is fruitless!”’
mn13:9.4: ‘Now this danger too in the case of sensual deisres … the reason being simply sensual desires.
mn13:10.1: ‘If property comes to the clansman while he works and strives and makes efforts thus,
mn13:10.2: he experiences pain and grief in protecting it:
mn13:10.3: “How shall neither kings nor thieves make off with my property nor fire burn it nor water sweep it away nor hateful heirs make off with it?”
mn13:10.4: And as he guards and protects his property, kings or thieves make off with it or fire burns it or water sweeps it away or hateful heirs make off with it.
mn13:10.5: And he sorrows, grieves and laments, beating his breast he weeps till he is distraught, (crying):
mn13:10.6: “What I had I have no more.”
mn13:10.7: ‘Now this danger too in the case of sensual desires … the reason being simply sensual desires.
mn13:11.1: ‘Again, with sensual desires for the reason, sensual desires for the source, sensual desires for the cause, the reason being simply sensual desires, kings quarrel with kings, warrior-nobles with warrior-nobles, divines with divines, householders with householders, mother with child, child with mother, father with child, child with father, brother with brother, brother with sister, friend with friend.
mn13:11.2: And here in their quarrels, brawls and disputes they attack each other with fists or with clods or with sticks or with knives,
mn13:11.3: whereby they incur death or deadly suffering.
mn13:11.4: ‘Now this danger too in the case of sensual desires … the reason being simply sensual desires.
mn13:12.1: ‘Again, with sensual desires for the reason … (men) take swords and shields and buckle on bows and quivers, and they charge into battle massed in double array with arrows and spears flying and swords flashing;
mn13:12.2: and there they are wounded by arrows and spears, and their heads are cut off by swords,
mn13:12.3: whereby they incur death or deadly suffering.
mn13:12.4: ‘Now this danger too in the case of sensual desires … the reason is simply sensual desires.
mn13:13.1: ‘Again, with sensual desires for the reason … (men) take swords, and shields and buckle on bows and quivers, and they charge slippery bastions, with arrows and spears flying, and swords flashing;
mn13:13.2: and there they are wounded by arrows and spears and splashed with boiling liquids and crushed under heavy weights, and their heads are cut off by swords,
mn13:13.3: whereby they incur death or deadly suffering.
mn13:13.4: ‘Now this danger too in the case of sensual desires … the reason is simply sensual desires.
mn13:14.1: ‘Again, with sensual desires for the reason … (men) break in and steal, turn bandit, rob highways, seduce others’ wives;
mn13:14.2: so that when they are caught, kings have many kinds of torture inflicted on them.
mn13:14.3: They have them flogged with whips, beaten with canes, beaten with clubs, they have their hands cut off, their feet cut off, their hands and feet cut off, their ears cut off, their noses cut off, their ears and noses cut off, they have them subjected to the “porridge-pot”, to the “polished-shell shave”, to the “eclipse’s mouth”, to the “fiery wreath”, to the “fiery hand”, to the “blades of grass”, to the “bark dress”, to the “antelope”, to the “meat-hooks”, to the “coins”, to the “lye-pickling”, to the “pivotting-pin”, to the “rolled-up palliasse”, and they have them splashed with boiling oil, and they have them thrown to dogs to devour, and they have them impaled alive on stakes, and they have their heads cut off with swords—
mn13:14.4: whereby they incur death or deadly suffering.
mn13:14.5: ‘Now this danger too in the case of sensual desires … the reason is simply sensual desires.
mn13:15.1: ‘Again, with sensual desires for the reason, sensual desires for the source, sensual desires for the cause, the reason being simply sensual desires, (men) indulge in misconduct of body, speech and mind:
mn13:15.2: on the dissolution of the body, after death, they reappear in states of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell.
mn13:15.3: ‘Now this danger too in the case of sensual desires, this mass of suffering in life to come, has sensual desires for its reason, sensual desires for its source, sensual desires for its cause, the reason being simply sensual desires.
mn13:16.1: (iii) ‘And what is escape in the case of sensual desires?
mn13:16.2: It is the removal of lustful desire, the abandonment of lustful desire, for sensual pleasures. ‘This is the escape in the case of sensual desires.
mn13:17.1: ‘That those monks and divines who do not understand, as it actually is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger and the escape as escape, in the case of sensual desires, can either themselves fully know sensual desires or instruct so that another can fully know sensual desires—that is not possible.
mn13:17.2: ‘That those monks and divines who understand, as it actually is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger and the escape as escape, in the case of sensual desires, can either themselves fully know sensual desires or instruct so that another can fully know sensual desires—that is possible.
mn13:18.1: (i) ‘And what is the gratification in the case of form?
mn13:18.2: ‘Suppose there were a girl of warrior-noble caste or divine caste or householder stock, in her fifteenth or sixteenth year, neither too tall nor too short, neither too thin nor too fat, neither too dark nor too fair: is her beauty and loveliness then at its height?’
mn13:18.4: ‘Now the pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on that beauty and loveliness are
mn13:18.5: the gratification in the case of form.
mn13:19.1: (ii) ‘And what is the danger in the case of form?
mn13:19.2: ‘Later on one might see that same woman here at eighty, ninety or a hundred years, aged, as crooked as a roof, doubled up, tottering with the aid of sticks, frail, her youth gone, her teeth broken, grey-haired, scanty-haired, bald, wrinkled, with limbs all blotchy:
mn13:19.3: how do you conceive this, bhikkhus,
mn13:19.4: has her former beauty and loveliness vanished and the danger become evident ?’
mn13:19.6: ‘Bhikkhus, this is the danger in the case of form.
mn13:20.1: ‘Again, one might see that same woman afflicted, suffering and gravely ill, lying fouled in her own excrement and urine, lifted up by some and set down by others.
mn13:20.2: How do you conceive this, bhikkhus,
mn13:20.3: has the former beauty and loveliness vanished and the danger become evident ?’
mn13:20.5: ‘Bhikkhus, this too is the danger in the case of form.
mn13:21.1: ‘Again, one might see that same woman as a corpse thrown on the charnel ground,
mn13:21.2: one-day dead, two-days dead, three-days dead, bloated, livid and oozing with matter.
mn13:21.3: How do you conceive this, bhikkhus,
mn13:21.4: has the former beauty and loveliness vanished and the danger become evident?’
mn13:21.6: ‘Bhikkhus, this too is the danger in the case of form.
mn13:22.1: ‘Again, one might see that same woman as a corpse thrown on a charnel ground,
mn13:22.2: devoured by crows, kites, vultures, dogs, jackals and various kinds of worms.
mn13:22.5: … the danger in the case of form.
mn13:23-28.2:
‘… a skeleton with flesh and blood held together by sinews …

‘… a fleshless skeleton smeared with blood and held together by sinews …

‘… a skeleton without flesh or blood held together by sinews …

‘… bones without sinews, scattered in all directions,
mn13:23-28.3: here a hand-bone there a foot-bone, there a shin-bone, there a thigh-bone, there a hip-bone, there the back-bone, there the skull …
mn13:29.1: Again, one might see that same woman as a corpse thrown on a charnel ground:
mn13:29.2: bones bleached white, the colour of shells … bones heaped up, more than a year old … bones rotted and crumbled to dust.
mn13:29.3: How do you conceive this, bhikkhus,
mn13:29.4: has the former beauty and loveliness vanished and the danger become evident?’
mn13:29.6: ‘Bhikkhus, this too is the danger in the case of form.’
mn13:30.1: (iii) ‘And what is escape in the case of form?
mn13:30.2: It is the removal of lustful desire, the abandonment of lustful desire, for form.’ ‘This is the escape in the case of form.’
mn13:31.1: ‘That those monks and divines who do not understand, as it actually is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger and the escape as escape, in the case of form, can either themselves fully know or instruct so that another can fully know form—that is not possible.’
mn13:32.1: (i) ‘And what is the gratification in the case of feelings?
mn13:32.2: ‘Here, bhikkhus, quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unprofitable dhammas, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained application, with happiness and pleasure born of seclusion.
mn13:32.3: ‘On such an occasion he does not choose for his own affliction, or for another’s affliction, or for the affliction of both.
mn13:32.4: On that occasion he feels only feeling that is free from affliction.
mn13:32.5: Gratification in the case of feeling in its highest aspect is freedom from affliction, I say.
mn13:33-35.1: ‘Again, with the stilling of initial and sustained application, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the second jhāna, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without initial application and sustained application, with happiness and pleasure born of concentration. ‘On such an occasion … freedom from affliction, I say.
mn13:33-35.2: ‘With the fading as well of happiness a bhikkhu abides in equanimity, mindful and fully aware, feeling pleasure with his body he enters upon and abides in the third jhāna, on account of which Noble Ones announce: “He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.”’ ‘On such an occasion … freedom from affliction, I say.
mn13:33-35.3: ‘With the abandoning of pleasure and pain and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. ‘On such an occasion he does not choose for his own affliction, or for another’s affliction, or for the affliction of both.
mn13:33-35.4: On that occasion he feels only feeling that is free from affliction.
mn13:33-35.5: Gratification in the case of feeling in its highest aspect is freedom from affliction, I say.
mn13:36.1: (ii) ‘And what is the danger in the case of feelings?
mn13:36.2: ‘Feelings are impermanent, painful, and inseparable from changefulness. ‘This is the danger in the case of feelings.
mn13:37.1: (iii) ‘And what is the escape in the case of feelings?
mn13:37.2: ‘It is the remove of lustful desire, the abandonment of lustful desire, for feelings. ‘This is the escape in the case of feelings.
mn13:38.1: ‘That those monks and divines who do not understand, as it actually is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape, in the case of feelings, can either themselves fully know feelings or instruct so that another can fully know feelings—that is not possible.
mn13:38.2: ‘That these monks and divines who understand, as it actually is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger and the escape as escape, in the case of feelings, can either themselves fully know feelings or instruct so that another can fully know feelings—that is possible.’
mn13:38.3: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn13:38.4: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
